newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed almost unchanged at 8.2920 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2919 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a lack of fresh market-moving news, traders said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2919.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2916 and moved in a range between the opening price and 8.2920 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2910 and a low of 8.2921. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2920, traders said.
Traders said the yuan had moved in a narrow range around 8.2920 since Monday due to a lack of market-moving news.
"The yuan won some support due to buying around the 8.2920 level but buyers seemed to have no intention of pushing up the yuan on the absence of any news," one traders said.
"The market was afraid of possible central bank intervention to depress the yuan because it is so high," a second trader said. "This made buying cautious and trading dull."

Traders said the market had now begun focussing on the annoucement due this weekend of China's foreign trade statistics for May. That data would be a key factor affecting the yuan's movements in the next few trading days, they said.
Traders said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2920 level on Thursday.
The yuan closed down at 7.3516 from 7.3166 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday high of 1.0700 from 1.0717 against the Hong Kong dollar.
